feature: A text box says how tall it turned out
summary: The H field for a piece of text used to be blank. It now shows the height the words actually came out to, dimmed, and it follows every re-wrap. You still cannot type into it.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Nothing to turn on.

try.do: Pick the text tool and click on a blank canvas.
Type "Sign in to continue to your account" and press Command-Return.
Read the Position & Size section: H says 21 in grey, where it used to say nothing.
Switch to the select tool and drag the right edge of the label leftwards until the words wrap onto three lines.
Read H again: it has grown to 55 on its own.
Click into H and try to type a number. Nothing lands, the same as before.
Hover H and read the tip: "Height follows the text. Change the width to re-wrap it, or the font size in the Text section."
Type 400 into W and press Return: H drops back to 21 as the words fall onto one line.

evaluate: Is a grey number in a normal-looking field enough to say you cannot type here, or does it read as broken?
When you click H and nothing happens, do you know why without hovering for the tip?
Is the height the number you actually wanted off a wrapped paragraph, or were you after the line height or the line count?
Should the same treatment reach the other numbers you cannot type: a locked layer's four, a stacked row's X and Y, a component copy's size?
rough: H still wears the same rounded box as the fields you can type in. Only the grey tells you apart, and a box that looks like an input but refuses the keyboard is the clumsiest part of this. Losing its border would say it louder, but that is a visual call worth your eye first.
Clicking a read-only field gives no feedback at all. The tip explains it, but only after a hover delay.
A line, an arrow and a caliper still show nothing for W and H on purpose: their box is padding around a stroke, so a width there would be a number about nothing you drew.

The same change makes a locked layer and a stacked row report their numbers too, instead of four blanks. That is covered by tests but is not in the screenshots here: a walk that tried to build a stack did not get one, so only the text case was photographed live.
Screen Recording was granted for this run, so both shots are real captures of the window, not offscreen renders.
